title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: Why does this track's diagnosis run opposite to the HR business partner track's?
options: Because L&D professionals are more anxious about AI than business partners are
Because the business partner's core territory is among the least AI-penetrated parts of HR, while L&D's core craft is among the most — so the reassuring version of the diagnosis would be false here
Because L&D has more budget exposure than the business partner function
Because business partners were taught this material in 201 and L&D professionals were not
questions.explanation: The shape of the finding is the same in both tracks (where has AI actually landed) and it points in opposite directions. Telling this audience "you're not behind, calm down" would be comfortable and untrue.

questions.prompt: What does the seven-stage chain reveal that a list of L&D responsibilities doesn't?
options: Which stages require the most specialized training to perform
That the hours concentrate in the middle stages while the distinctive value concentrates at the two ends — so collapsing the middle promotes the ends to being the whole job
That delivery is the stage most exposed to automation
That the stages must be performed in strict sequence to be effective
questions.explanation: A responsibilities list is unordered and hides the asymmetry. Only a sequence shows that time and value sit in different places.

questions.prompt: In the triage, what does question one — "is it cheap now?", actually ask?
options: Whether the item was inexpensive to produce originally
Whether the item is low quality
What it would cost to replace the item today, regardless of what it cost to make
Whether the item is still being used by the business
questions.explanation: What it cost you is a fact about the past. The triage is about replacement cost now, which is why "but that took my team six weeks" isn't an answer to it.

questions.prompt: Why does the module insist the three questions be run in order?
options: Because the buckets must be equally sized for the analysis to work
Because running question three first makes everything look human-critical, and running question one first without the later rescues would swallow work that genuinely belongs in two or three
Because questions two and three are harder and should be attempted when fresh
Because the order matches the sequence of the chain in Lesson 1
questions.explanation: Both failure modes are real and they point in opposite directions. The discipline is a harsh question one followed by honest rescues, not a gentle pass through all three.

questions.prompt: What actually protects the material in bucket two?
options: That the judgment involved is too subtle for a model to reproduce
That it is legally restricted from being processed by AI systems
That the information it depends on is undocumented — absent from any record a model could have been trained on
That it changes too frequently for a model's knowledge cutoff
questions.explanation: And the distinction matters enormously, because the undocumented-information claim comes with a condition: it holds only while the information stays undocumented. The subtlety claim would be permanent, and it isn't the one the module makes.

questions.prompt: According to the module, what would most shrink bucket two?
options: A substantially more capable model
Your own organization getting better at documenting how it actually works
Vendors gaining access to more industry-specific training data
A reduction in the regulatory constraints on AI in employment
questions.explanation: Which is uncomfortable, because that is normally considered an unambiguously good thing to do. A is the answer that skips the mechanism: the constraint is the record, not the reasoning.

questions.prompt: Why does the module state what the track won't teach?
options: To set expectations about the time commitment involved
Because those topics are covered in optional supplementary material
Because building content with AI is 201 M3, a standards pack is 201 M2, and a calendar of workflows is 201 M7 — a 300-level course that re-teaches them is charging twice for the same material
Because production topics are outside the scope of any 301 track
questions.explanation: They are the three most obvious modules a Talent Development course would reach for, which is exactly why they need naming. D is wrong: other tracks teach production-adjacent craft where the role makes it specialist.

questions.prompt: A learner reports they can't produce an inventory of their own catalog. How should that be treated?
options: As a failure to complete the activity, which should be resubmitted once the list exists
As a finding about the function that is worth more than the exercise, and which should become the write-up
As a reason to run the triage on a hypothetical portfolio instead
As evidence that the function is too small for the triage to apply
questions.explanation: A function that can't enumerate what it publishes has learned something structural about itself. The activity is a means of finding things out; when the means fails informatively, the finding is the output.
